events_chronological: As a young woman, Meilin defies her father Renjie to emigrate overseas with Bao.
Meilin and Bao open a laundromat, and every other life she might have had closes off one by one.
Their daughter Junie grows up feeling judged, and Meilin cannot bring herself to accept her girlfriend Robin.
On the origin branch, a version of Meilin invents branch-jumping and pushes her own daughter's mind across every universe at once until it shatters, making the entity Kavra Nul.
Kavra Nul builds a black ring, a hole made of everything that ever mattered, and starts hunting for the Meilin who can face her.
In the laundromat, Meilin prepares for a tax audit while Bao tries and fails to hand her divorce papers.
Renjie arrives from overseas for the new year party, and Meilin hides Robin from him.
In the lift to the tax office, the origin-branch Bao takes over her husband's body and gives Meilin an earpiece and a set of instructions.
Meilin branch-jumps for the first time in a supply closet and fights the security guards with skills borrowed from a film-star version of herself.
The auditor Beulah Sneed turns berserk, and the tax office becomes a battlefield.
Meilin is shown the origin branch and told that Kavra Nul is her own daughter.
Meilin jumps through lives she never lived - film star, opera singer, teppanyaki chef, a world where people have hot dogs for fingers, two rocks on a cliff.
The origin-branch Bao is killed, and Meilin's mind begins to come apart as she jumps too far.
Meilin confronts Kavra Nul, who says she does not want to kill her but wants her to see that nothing matters.
Believing nothing matters, Meilin turns on the people around her and nearly follows her daughter into the ring.
Bao, in every universe at once, asks her to be kind, and Meilin starts fighting with kindness instead.
Meilin gives each attacker what they actually need, wins Renjie's acceptance of Robin, and reaches Junie at the edge of the ring.
Meilin tells Junie that even if nothing matters she would still choose to be here with her, and pulls her back.
Back at the tax office the family files the return together, and Meilin's attention drifts for a moment across every universe at once.
nonlinear_category_reason: The afternoon at the tax office holds 9 of 12 scenes and runs forward, and the emigration, the daughter's childhood and the origin branch all intrude from earlier.
syuzhet_notes: The present is one afternoon at a tax office, and everything else arrives as intrusion rather than flashback in the ordinary sense: told-order bullets 7-8 explain an origin in another universe, bullets 10-11 and 14 reach back into the protagonist's own past, and bullet 9 covers lives she never lived at all. From told-order bullet 9 the cutting accelerates until several universes occupy the same second.
fabula_notes: Most of the alternate universes are not events on one timeline but branches that never happened to this version of the protagonist, so a strict chronology can place only the ones that bear on her, in the order the film establishes them as causes. The origin-branch history is recounted in dialogue rather than dramatised in sequence.
